$comment: The notification Shortcut: how to set it up (settings/shortcut.tsx), its settings (automation.tsx) and the log of what it could not read (parselog.tsx). Names in quotes are Apple's Shortcuts app labels and the Kopiyka action's name — use the names iOS shows in the target language.

settings.title: Shortcut settings
settings.silent: It logs the payment and says nothing
settings.granted: One notification per payment, replacing the last one
settings.denied: Notifications are off in the Settings app, so it stays silent
settings.ask: Allow notifications and it will say what it logged
settings.openSettingsSubtitle: Notifications are turned off for Kopiyka

notifyShort.message: One notification at a time. The app icon’s badge counts entries waiting for approval.
notifyShort.note: Footnote under the notification setting; the ⓘ unfolds notifyMore.

notifyMore.message: A new payment replaces the previous notification, so nothing piles up, and it goes away once the entry is opened or approved. It says whether the shop was recognised, guessed or not known at all, and when a transfer between your accounts was matched. Tapping it opens the entry.

logMissed.message: {count, plural, one {# notification could not be turned into a transaction} other {# notifications could not be turned into a transaction}}
logMissed.note: Subtitle of the Notification log row.

logHintShort.message: Notifications it could not read are kept here, with their text. Exports as CSV.
logHintShort.note: Footnote under the Notification log row; the ⓘ unfolds logHintMore.

logHintMore.message: A bank whose wording it does not know yet loses purchases quietly; the saved text is what the reading gets fixed from.

shortcut.title: Automate with Shortcut
shortcut.intro: Your bank already notifies you about every payment. Pass that notification to Kopiyka and it logs the payment for you. Set it up once.

needsOld.message: Needs iOS {version} or later — this device runs iOS {current}. Everything else in Kopiyka works as it is.
needsOld.note: version is "26"; current is the device's iOS, "18.5".

needsUnknown.message: Needs iOS {version} or later. Everything else in Kopiyka works as it is.

step1.note: Apple's Shortcuts app, then its + button.

step1Sub.message: Open Shortcuts and tap + at the bottom. If it asks you to describe a shortcut, tap Edit.
step1Sub.note: Edit is the Shortcuts button at the top right of the “Describe a shortcut” screen (only with Apple Intelligence).

step2.note: Shortcuts labels: the Automation chip, then the Notification trigger.

shortcut.step2Sub: Tap Automation under the search field, then search for Notification.

step3Sub.message: Tap App and search for it. No bank notifications? Pick Wallet (Apple Pay); + adds a second app.
step3Sub.note: App is the trigger's placeholder in Shortcuts.

step4.note: Message and contains are Shortcuts labels.

step4Sub.message: Add Filter, change Title to Message, and type a word every payment notification has, like “Amount”.
step4Sub.note: Add Filter, Title, Message: Shortcuts labels. The example is a word banks print; use one natural for the language's banks.

shortcut.step5: Let it run on its own

step5Sub.message: Tap the arrow beside the app: keep Automation on and Notify off.
step5Sub.note: Automation and Notify are Shortcuts switches.

step6.message: Add “Log payment from an app notification”
step6.note: The Kopiyka action's name exactly as Shortcuts lists it (native.json intents.payment.title).

step6Sub.message: Search for Kopiyka in the field at the bottom.
step6Sub.note: Kopiyka is what to type; keep it in Latin letters.

step7Sub.message: Tap Notification, then Select Variable, then the Notification under the trigger.
step7Sub.note: Select Variable is a Shortcuts button; Notification is the trigger's variable.

step8Sub.message: Tap the arrow, then Location → Choose → Current Location → ✓. Leave Account empty: Kopiyka picks it from the card or the currency.
step8Sub.note: Location, Account: the Kopiyka action's fields; Choose, Current Location: Shortcuts labels.

step9Sub.message: It saves itself. You’ll find it in Library → Automation, where its switch turns it off.
step9Sub.note: Library and Automation are Shortcuts labels.

bankApp.note: Label on the guide picture where Messages stands in for the bank's app (the simulator has none).

edit.note: Label under Shortcuts' Edit button on the guide picture of the “Describe a shortcut” screen, which only exists in English (Apple Intelligence). Use the name Shortcuts gives the button in this language.

step.note: Accessibility label of a step's pictures; n is the step number.

shortcut.unavailableMessage: Install the Shortcuts app from the App Store, then come back.
shortcut.pendingSub: Check the category once and approve.
shortcut.knownSub: Same category and tags as last time.
shortcut.accountSub: Picked from the card, or the currency.
shortcut.onlySub: Codes, deliveries and declined payments are ignored.
shortcut.settingsSub: Notifications, and anything it could not read.
shortcut.hint: Works with Kopiyka closed. Nothing leaves your phone.

log.title: Notification log
log.intro: Notifications the automation could not turn into a transaction, newest first. None of this leaves the phone.

introMissed.message: Notifications the automation could not turn into a transaction, newest first. None of this leaves the phone. {count, plural, one {# may be a purchase that was missed.} other {# may be a purchase that was missed.}}
introMissed.note: As intro, plus how many entries may be lost purchases.

log.unreadableWhy: Money is named and no amount could be read out of it. This is the one worth working on.
log.failedWhy: Understood, but nothing was written — no account to put it on, or the app refused.
log.ignoredWhy: No amount in it, or money the bank is not charging: a balance, a code, a declined card. Usually right.

a11yShow.note: VoiceOver label; outcome is "Unreadable", when "14:32 · 15 Sep".

a11yHide.note: VoiceOver label; outcome is "Unreadable", when "14:32 · 15 Sep".

empty.note: Shown in place of a notification with no text.

field.note: A label before a value, "Shop: ". Keep the trailing space.

log.noneHint: Every notification the automation was handed became a transaction, or was not about money.
log.exportSub: One row per notification, the whole text included
log.exportSubCount: One row per notification, the whole text included · {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}
log.clearSub: Transactions it already wrote are not touched
log.clearMessage: The transactions it already wrote are not touched — only this record of what was read.
